activities.title: Shape Sorting Hunt
activities.description: Walk around the house together and find objects that match a shape you call out -- circle, square, triangle.
activities.example: Mia found a clock (circle) on the wall, a window (square), and a slice of toast (triangle)!
materials: None needed -- use objects already around the house
steps: Call out a shape, like "circle"
Race to find 3 things around the room shaped like it
Swap shapes and go again

activities.title: Memory Match
activities.description: Lay out pairs of matching cards face-down and take turns flipping two at a time to find pairs.
activities.example: Jayden remembered where the matching dinosaur cards were and got 4 pairs in a row.
materials: A deck of cards, or paper cut into matching pairs
steps: Lay 8-12 cards face-down in a grid
Each person flips two cards per turn
If they match, keep them; if not, flip back and pass the turn

activities.title: Copy My Pattern
activities.description: Clap a short rhythm or sequence of sounds and have your child copy it back, building the pattern longer each round.
activities.example: Dad clapped clap-clap-pause-clap, and Zoe copied it perfectly, then added one more clap.
steps: Clap a simple 2-3 beat pattern
Have your child repeat it exactly
Add one more beat each round they get right

activities.title: Grocery Math
activities.description: At the store or looking at a receipt, have your child estimate the total cost before you check out, then compare.
activities.example: Priya guessed the 5 items would total about $18 -- the real total was $19.40, close!
steps: Pick 5 items and ask them to round each price and add them up in their head
Check the real total together
Talk about how close the estimate was

activities.title: Spot the Difference
activities.description: Take two photos of the same room a few minutes apart after moving a few small objects, then have your child find what changed.
activities.example: Liam spotted that the remote moved and a cushion flipped over, but missed the moved mug.
steps: Photograph a room or table
Move 3-5 small objects while they're not looking
Photograph again and have them spot every change

activities.title: Treasure Map Logic
activities.description: Draw a simple grid map and hide a small prize, then give step-by-step directional clues for your child to follow.
activities.example: Noah followed "5 steps north, 3 steps east" and found the hidden sticker behind the couch.
materials: Paper, pencil, a small treat or toy
steps: Draw a grid of a room or yard
Hide something and mark clues like "3 steps north, 2 steps east"
Let them follow the clues to find it

activities.title: Strategy Game Night
activities.description: Play a strategy board or card game together and talk through the reasoning behind each move.
activities.example: Grandpa and Ethan played checkers, and Ethan explained why he was setting up a double-jump.
materials: Any strategy game -- chess, checkers, or a card game you own
steps: Pick a game that involves planning ahead
Before each move, ask them to explain their thinking out loud
After the game, talk about one move they'd replay differently

activities.title: Headline Detective
activities.description: Read a news headline together and guess what the article is about before reading it, then check how close the guess was.
activities.example: Before reading, Ava guessed an article about a "robot chef" was about a restaurant -- it was actually a cooking competition.
materials: A kid-appropriate news site or paper
steps: Pick a headline and cover the article
Predict what happened and why
Read the article and compare notes

activities.title: 20 Questions, Harder Mode
activities.description: Play 20 Questions but require every question to be a yes/no question that narrows down a category logically.
activities.example: Sam guessed "the Eiffel Tower" in 14 yes/no questions by narrowing down place, then country, then landmark.
steps: One person thinks of a person, place, or thing
The other asks only yes/no questions to narrow it down
Try to guess correctly before running out of questions

activities.title: Debate a Topic
activities.description: Pick a low-stakes topic and each take an opposing side, arguing your case for a few minutes before switching sides.
activities.example: Mom argued pineapple belongs on pizza, Jordan argued it doesn't -- then they swapped and argued the opposite side.
steps: Agree on a light topic (best pizza topping, ideal weekend)
Each person argues one side for 2 minutes
Switch sides and argue the opposite

activities.title: Budget a Fictional Trip
activities.description: Plan a fictional weekend trip together within a set budget, researching real costs for travel, food, and activities.
activities.example: Maya planned a $500 weekend in Seattle, finding a $120 train ticket, a cheap hostel, and one paid museum visit.
materials: Internet access, paper or a notes app
steps: Set a total budget and a destination
Look up realistic costs for transport, food, and one activity
Adjust the plan until it fits the budget

activities.title: Teach It Back
activities.description: Have your teen pick something they learned recently in school and explain it to you as if you knew nothing about it.
activities.example: Alex explained the water cycle to Dad using a cup of water and a plate to show evaporation and rain.
steps: Ask them to choose a recent school topic
Have them explain it simply, as if teaching a younger kid
Ask follow-up questions to deepen their explanation
